uncited: This family covers the storage, generation, and management of procedural noise data structures used in volume rendering.
It addresses the problem of efficiently providing high-frequency detail or base fields to shaders without excessive memory bandwidth or CPU overhead.

It differs from its siblings by focusing on the *mechanics* of data creation (CPU/GPU generation, texture formats, struct layouts) rather than the mathematical definition of the noise fields themselves.
**Gradient Assignment**: Each integer lattice point (vertex) in the domain is assigned a pseudo-random gradient vector $\mathbf{g}$.

**Smoothing/Fade Function**: To ensure smooth transitions ($C^1$ continuity), the fractional coordinates of $\mathbf{P}$ within the cell are passed through a fade function $f(t)$ before interpolation.
This variant emphasizes on-the-fly computation to optimize memory usage.
This variant defines a specific host-side data structure for configuring noise parameters.
Procedural noise generation has evolved from CPU-based texture synthesis to GPU-accelerated on-the-fly computation.
